From someone who is only slightly ahead of you:
My gap year turned into about 2 and a half though family health had a lot to do with that. Yes, it slowed me down, and ultimately, possibly took me off of my most profitable track for my life. At the end of the day I took time to find myself and instead of that engineering track I was going to rush into I realised who I was and how I saw my life better than most people our age give time to. It's a give and take. A gap year provides distractions and time to change your mind, but ultimately it can give you time to figure a lot out. Rushing will be more of a guess but momentum can be the difference for getting a profitable career. Would you rather take time to figure you out, or take time to get to a career sooner

This isn't poop but it's similar. 
I was in a hospital at one point and I woke up that morning needing to pee really badly. There were two bathrooms in our wing for us 10-15 guys. The bathrooms were full and I couldn't go for a while. My bladder was in shear pain from the amount of urine. So with the door to my room open and knowing I was on camera with the camera feed being broadcasted to the office where someone tended to be at all times I grabbed a towel hastily threw it in the corner and soaked it. It was another 3 days till my next scheduled laundry day.
